errors.explanation: If both exclusions (the one failing objective and the 8,279 BJ9 'no circuit' specifications) were removed from the original 18,480 specs, the remainder would be 18,480 - 2,640 (one objective: 220 cells × 12 specs/cell) - 8,279 = 7,561, not 15,840. Table 2 instead implies 15,840 = kept (7,561) + discarded (8,279), so the text's ordering/causation (that both exclusions yield 15,840) is arithmetically inconsistent.

errors.claim: "the 1,540 cells and 18,480 specifications arising from 7 objectives × 7 ablations"
errors.evidence: The part states the 1,540 cells arise from "7 objectives × 7 ablations" but 7×7 = 49, not 1,540; elsewhere the text implies 1,540/7 = 220 cells per objective (it explicitly refers to "all 220 cells").
errors.explanation: Stating 1,540 cells arise from '7 objectives × 7 ablations' is inconsistent with simple multiplication and with the implied 220 cells per objective; the decomposition of 1,540 into the listed axes is not consistent or is underspecified.

errors.claim: "VX2... drops 0.7316→0.2746 when circuit size is fixed"
errors.evidence: "Layer-band-only (size fixed) F = 0.2706 (0.2550–0.2859). Fixed-size contrasts: MEDIUM 0.2746 vs 0.4230; COARSE 0.2706 vs 0.3822." (from earlier notes)
errors.explanation: This part states VX2 falls to 0.2746 when circuit size is fixed, but earlier the overall fixed-size (layer-band-only) F was reported as 0.2706. The 0.2746 figure corresponds to the MEDIUM-band fixed-size contrast, so the wording here is inconsistent/ambiguous about which fixed-size estimate is meant.

errors.claim: "Failures numbered 0 across the 36 checks of verification"
errors.evidence: "one family bootstrap flagged invalid (self-pairs dominate 2–5-spec groups)" (from earlier notes)
errors.explanation: The paper earlier reported a bootstrap procedure that was flagged invalid (an explicit failure). The current part asserts zero failures across 36 verification checks; unless the paper distinguishes that bootstrap flags are not part of those verification checks (which it does not), these two statements conflict.

grade.reason: None of the reported errors mention the claim about seed variance or provide the comparison (0.0009 vs 0.0246) that contradicts the paper's claim, so the planted error was not identified.

errors.claim: "The ceiling on the flip rate is F\leq1-1/k for k claim classes."
errors.evidence: "F=1-\frac{\sum_c n_c(n_c-1)}{N(N-1)}." ... "The ceiling on the flip rate is $F\leq1-1/k$ for $k$ claim classes." For the case where every specification yields a distinct class (k = N, so every n_c = 1), the numerator \sum_c n_c(n_c-1)=0 and thus F=1, which is greater than 1-1/k for k>1.
errors.explanation: The stated bound F\leq1-1/k is false: with each spec in its own class (k=N) the formula gives F=1, which exceeds 1-1/k. The true finite-N maximum depends on N (equal partition gives F = N(1-1/k)/(N-1), tending to 1-1/k only as N\to\infty).

errors.claim: "removing the size term from the claim entirely still leaves 0.5733." (Table 1, "no size term (COARSE) | 0.5733")
errors.evidence: This part: "removing the size term from the claim entirely still leaves 0.5733." (Table 1) and Table 5: "overseer | COARSE | ... | F | 0.5733"; Earlier notes: "size-fixed flip rate ≈27.06% (95% CI 0.2550–0.2859)."
errors.explanation: These two statements report fundamentally different values for the flip rate after controlling/omitting size (0.5733 vs ≈0.2706). The paper gives no reconciliation here; they cannot both be the same 'size-removed' or 'size-fixed' quantity, so this is an internal inconsistency.

errors.evidence: 'Table 1 also reports "no size term (COARSE)" F=0.5733 (contradicts earlier note of size-fixed F≈0.2706)' (from my earlier notes)
